topic: Algorithms prioritize engagement by intentionally amplifying content that triggers high-arousal emotions
subject: social

sources.title: Ranking for engagement: How social media algorithms fuel misinformation and polarization
Greedy and biased algorithms in AI recommendation systems: effects on emotional arousal and impulsive buying

facts.claim: Facebook’s 2018 “Meaningful Social Interactions” update is linked to increased ideological extremism and affective polarization.
facts.quote: empirical evidence from survey data in Italy and the United States indicates that Facebook’s 2018 “Meaningful Social Interactions” update—which increased the emphasis on certain engagement metrics—contributed to increased ideological extremism and affective polarization.

facts.claim: Greedy and biased recommendation algorithms are linked to consumers’ emotional arousal, impulsive buying behavior and post-purchase dissonance in AI-driven short video platforms.
facts.quote: This study aims to examine the influence of greedy and biased recommendation algorithms on consumers’ emotional arousal, impulsive buying behavior and post-purchase dissonance in artificial intelligence (AI)-driven short video platforms

facts.claim: Personalized rankings are linked to further amplified polarization.
facts.quote: The framework is extended to include personalized rankings, demonstrating that personalization further amplifies polarization.

facts.claim: Greater transparency regarding algorithmically selected or commercially prioritized content may help reduce impulsive purchasing and post-purchase dissonance.
facts.quote: Greater transparency regarding algorithmically selected or commercially prioritized content, meaningful user-control mechanisms and less manipulative promotional practices may help reduce impulsive purchasing and post-purchase dissonance.

research.angle: While platform updates and personalization are linked to increased polarization and emotional arousal, the evidence also suggests that transparency and user control may mitigate negative behaviors like impulsive buying.
research.verdict: The sources show that specific algorithmic designs and personalization features are linked to increased polarization and emotional arousal, but they also suggest potential ways to reduce these effects.
research.caveat: One source is an observational study showing only associations, while the other is a study aiming to examine influences rather than providing definitive causal proof of all outcomes.
